notes: Read against the maker's source at tag v2.6.13, commit 00f3497, which is the installed version; the branch has since moved to 2.6.14. Three manuals were used alongside it: the repository README, docs/modules/Metriks/Manual.md, and docs/modules/RKD/Manual.pdf, an 18-page PDF read with pypdf. Every module in the plugin carries a Model submenu offering Creamy, Stage Repro, Absolute Night, Dark "Signature", Deepblue "Signature" and Titanium "Signature", plus silver or gold jacks and screws to match; it changes nothing but appearance, so under the house rule it gets no line except on the six blank panels, where being looked at is the module's whole function. RKD and BRK do not have that submenu: they follow Rack's own Use dark panels if available setting instead. A new module of any other kind comes up as Absolute Night when that Rack setting is on and Creamy when it is off, and then keeps whichever model it was given. SHARED GROUND WITH OhmerPrems, which is closed source and not in this batch: KlokSpid MkII in that plugin is the direct successor to this KlokSpid and the README says it is free and unlimited, so the SETUP system described here, the encoder-plus-button interface, the 31-entry ratio list and the output-level choices are the conventions to expect there. The six-model theme scheme and the silver-or-gold jack swap are almost certainly shared too, and the same house rule should leave them out of the lines. The RKD and BRK pairing may recur as well, since OhmerPrems continues the same maker's expander habits.

Turning it clockwise moves to the next mode and anticlockwise to the previous one; while an option is being edited it moves through that option's choices instead. It has no end stops

Metriks.notes: The PLAY/PAUSE button and the PLAY/PAUSE jack are both dead as shipped. They are declared at src/Metriks.cpp:18 and :24 and configured at :216 and :219, and nothing else in the file reads either; the maker's own manual says they are reserved for a Peak Counter mode that is not written. Both get a line saying so, because an untagged control falls back to the maker's tooltip, which would promise a function. The RESET button and jack are read at :920 and only do anything in the voltmeter's Minimum, Maximum and Median settings (:922-930); in CV Pitch they do nothing. The OUT jack is a straight copy of IN on one channel (:742). The input is read with plain getVoltage, so a polyphonic cable is measured on its first channel only. The encoder is configured with infinite limits at :214 and is read as a delta at :746. The 10-second option timeout is at :1013. The Model submenu is on every module in this plugin and is left out per the house rule; it is listed once in the plugin-level notes.

lines: A clock generator and clock multiplier or divider driven from a display, four outputs each with their own ratio

With no cable in CLK it sets the tempo in beats per minute; with a clock patched it chooses the ratio from a list running from divide by 64 to multiply by 64. Inside SETUP it moves through the choices
Held down for about two seconds it opens or closes SETUP; inside SETUP a short press moves to the next setting, and outside it starts and stops the generated clock
The clock this module follows; with a cable here the module multiplies or divides it instead of generating its own tempo. A rising edge is counted above 1.7V and the input rearms below 0.2V

KlokSpid.notes: The README declares this module deprecated and says it cannot be added from the module browser; the installed plugin.json carries no hidden flag for it and src/Ohmer.cpp:22 registers it normally, so it does appear in the browser. That is worth a person checking in the running Rack. Only two of the module's controls exist as parameters: the encoder at src/KlokSpid.cpp:332, configured with infinite limits, and the button at :333-334. Everything else is a SETUP page drawn on the display and driven by those two, which means no other setting can be reached by clicking, and the right-click menu holds only the Model submenu. The ratio list is the 31 values at :107, running from 64 down to 1/64. The CV mapping is at :987-993: the clamped voltage is multiplied by 12.6 and rounded, which is what steps it through the list. Output level choices are at :561-578 and the option to put an LFO waveform on the fourth jack at :1272-1285, available only while that jack is at ratio x1. Because SETUP is a screen rather than a set of controls, the settings it holds are written as Note lines and only the ones that could be read straight from the source are given.

lines: A clock divider with eight outputs, each on its own ratio, and a control voltage that rotates which ratio each output carries
One of the six jumpers on the circuit board; installed, the outputs count down-beat and all eight fire on the first clock pulse. Removed, they count up-beat, each firing after its own count
One of the six jumpers; installed, the outputs hold a gate that changes state on each count. Removed, they send a short trigger
One of the six jumpers, and one of the two that set the largest divider between them: with both installed the largest is 8, with both removed 64, and with this one alone removed 32
One of the six jumpers, and one of the two that set the largest divider between them: with both installed the largest is 8, with both removed 64, and with this one alone removed 16
One of the six jumpers; installed, the dividers are spread across the whole range the two Max Div jumpers allow instead of bunching at the low end
One of the six jumpers; installed, the module resets itself every time twice the largest divider has been counted, which brings odd dividers back into step
A steady voltage from 0V to 5V rotates the table, moving every output onto a different ratio; negative voltages and an unpatched jack count as 0V, and anything above 5V counts as 5V
A rising edge above 3.5V restarts the count on every output; the jack rearms below 0.2V
The clock every output divides, counted on a rising edge above 3.5V and rearmed below 0.2V; with nothing patched here all eight displays read two dashes and the lamp by RESET turns red
A 5V trigger or gate at the ratio the display beside it shows
Note — the six jumpers are hidden until you tick Access jumpers (located on PCB) in the right-click menu, which turns the panel into a circuit board; the panel shows nothing of them otherwise
Note — the module does nothing at all until a clock is patched into CLK
Note — the two-digit display beside each output jack shows that output's current divider and follows the rotation as it changes
Note — the lamp beside the RESET jack is red when no clock is patched, orange on a reset arriving at the jack, and blue on a reset the module gave itself
Note — the Max Div and Spread jumpers apply only to the Manufacturer table; the other four tables ignore them
Note — with Max Div at 8 and Spread installed the largest divider becomes 16 and the eight ratios come out as triplets and sixteenths, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16
Note — a BRK expander placed against either side of this module drives these six jumpers from switches, so the circuit board never has to be opened

Menu — Dividers table: Manufacturer, Prime numbers, Perfect squares, Fibonacci sequence, Triplet & 16ths — chooses the eight ratios the outputs start from

RKD.notes: The six parameters are jumpers drawn on a circuit-board view of the panel, hidden until the menu item is ticked (src/RKD.cpp:997-1002 for the item, :1137-1142 for the hiding). They are at src/RKD.cpp:1107-1123 in left-to-right order, so index 0 is J1 and index 5 is J6, matching the manual's numbering. The Max Div table is at :324-332: both Max Div jumpers installed gives 8, Max Div 32 removed gives 16, Max Div 16 removed gives 32, both removed gives 64, and the pair with Spread installed gives 16. Extra tables force Max Div to 64 at :334. Auto-reset fires at twice the largest divider (:708, :767). The RESET lamp colours are at :785-810; the manual calls the third colour purple in one place and the code names the light PURPLE while the comment calls it blue. Clock and reset thresholds are 3.5V rising and 0.2V falling (:590, :645, :671), matching the manual. The eight outputs are genuinely identical in function and differ only by their ratio, so one line covers them and all eight tags point at it; the panel prints each one as 1+R through 8+R and each carries its own display. The ROTATE jack is not a pitch or a gate input: it is a stepped selector read as a level, which is why it is given the cv family.

lines: A panel of six switches that sets the jumpers of an RKD placed immediately to its left or its right, so the circuit board never has to be opened
COUNTING to the right, under the down arrow, makes the RKD count down-beat, with all eight outputs firing together on the first clock pulse; to the left they count up-beat
TRIG. GATE to the right makes the RKD hold a gate on each output; to the left it sends a short trigger
One of the two MAX DIV switches: with both to the right the largest divider is 8, with both to the left it is 64, and with this one alone to the left it is 16
One of the two MAX DIV switches: with both to the right the largest divider is 8, with both to the left it is 64, and with this one alone to the left it is 32
SPREAD to ON spreads the RKD's dividers across the whole range the MAX DIV switches allow; to OFF they bunch at the low end
AUTO-RESET to ON makes the RKD reset itself every time twice the largest divider has been counted
Note — this panel does nothing unless an RKD is placed against it, on either side, with no gap; it has no jacks, no lamps and no power draw
Note — with an RKD on both sides the one on the right is driven and the one on the left is left alone
Note — the switch positions are copied into the RKD's jumpers every sample, so the RKD's own jumpers cannot be moved by hand while this panel is attached
Note — MAX DIV and SPREAD reach the RKD only while it is using its Manufacturer dividers table; the other four tables ignore both
Note — once the RKD is set the way you need it, this panel can be removed and the setting stays
BRK.notes: The six switches are sent to the RKD at src/BRK.cpp:54-77, once for an RKD on the left and once for one on the right, with the left-hand case tested first so it wins. The two Max Div switches are deliberately crossed on the way out (:59-60): the switch the code calls SWITCH_MAXDIVRANGE32 drives the RKD's Max Div 16 jumper and vice versa, which compensates for the two being drawn in the opposite order (:128-130) from the jumpers' left-to-right order on the RKD board. The result on the panel is what the printing says, and it matches the manual: both switches left gives 64, both right gives 8. The parameter tooltips do not: the switch tooltipped Max Div 16 is the one the panel marks 32 on the left, and the switch tooltipped Max Div 32 is the one marked 16. Because the RKD's parameters are written every sample from here, moving a jumper on the RKD itself has no lasting effect while a BRK is attached.
